title: Output Schema Versioning and Walkback Playbook
author: Leah Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood's recommended approach for evolving model output schemas, negotiating versions between clients and runtime, and performing an automated "walkback" (safe rollback with stateful validation and postmortem hooks) when schema incompatibilities cause customer-impacting failures. It applies to hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes and complements the API compatibility and deprecation policy.

Goals

- Limit visible breaking changes in outputs to <0.01% of active tokens served per month.
- Detect and contain schema regressions within 15 minutes of rollout, with automated rollback for severe regressions.
- Provide clear remediation paths and observability (telemetry, traces, and example-request capture) for customers and SRE.

Scope

Applies to: model-serving responses (text generation JSON envelope, structured-tool outputs, embeddings/metadata payloads) produced by services: runtime-router, model-loader, generation-worker, and response-formatter. Does NOT change input prompt semantics or API routing rules (see API-deprecation doc).

Compatibility model (summary)

1) Semantic minor versions (vMAJOR.MINOR):
   - MAJOR change: incompatible removal or rename of top-level fields (requires documented migration & canary).
   - MINOR change: additive, non-breaking fields or explicit opt-in flags.
2) Backwards-compatibility rules: clients must tolerate unknown top-level fields and must read using declared output type fields rather than position-dependent arrays.

Version negotiation rules (runtime-router)

- Default behavior: runtime advertises the active schema version in response metadata header X-Redwood-Output-Schema: v1.3.
- Clients may send Accept-Output-Schema: v1.2,v1.3 to indicate preference list. The runtime will select the highest compatible version that satisfies both sides.
- If no overlap, runtime returns HTTP 406 with a structured error and a brief example of available schema fields.

Observability and SLOs

- Schema mismatch rate (SLO): <= 0.1% requests/hour for stable models; alert when > 0.05% sustained for 10 minutes to paging channel SRE-Model-Alerts.
- Example-capture retention: store one failing request per unique client API key per hour (rotate after 30 days).
- Traces: ensure generation-worker spans include schema_validation:{result: pass|fail, details: short-string}.

Deployment and rollout checklist

1. Authoring and Validation (developer):
   - Update schema definition in /repo/serving/schemas/<model-name>/schema-v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.json (JSON-Schema Draft 2020-12).
   - Run local compatibility check: tools/schema-compat check --from v<prev> --to v<new>. This verifies additive-only fields for MINOR bumps or reports diffs for MAJOR bumps.
   - Add unit tests that deserialize representative request corpus (see tests/schema-corpus).

2. Preflight (CI):
   - CI runs batch of representative prompts (real anonymized sample or synthetic seed set) with schema validation enabled.
   - Gate: 0 failing schema validations allowed for a MINOR; for MAJOR, require manual approval by API-standards owner.

3. Canary (runtime-router + canary group):
   - Deploy model with schema vX.Y to canary pool (1–2% traffic) for 2 hours.
   - Monitor: schema_mismatch_rate, token_latency_95, example_capture_failures.
   - If schema_mismatch_rate > 0.01% or a customer-facing error >= P1 appears, trigger automated rollback.

4. Progressive rollout:
   - 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with metric checks at each step (10 minute steady-state window).

Walkback (automated rollback and containment)

Definition: walkback is the coordinated sequence that returns traffic away from a problematic model schema while preserving trace and sample evidence for analysis.

Trigger conditions (any of):
- schema_mismatch_rate > 0.1% for 5 minutes.
- API error rate from response-formatter >= 0.5% (client-visible errors).
- Manual SRE/PM request labeled urgent.

Walkback steps (automated):
1) runtime-router marks the offending model-version:status=draining and reroutes new requests to fallback-compatible variant (same family) or fallback model alias configured in model_catalog.
2) generation-worker emits finalization span and persists last-K KV cache snapshots for repro (K = 3 per shard).
3) telemetry-ingest creates a high-priority incident with attached example captures and trace URLs.
4) Automated rollback job (walkback-runner) flips active alias to last-known-good model-version and validates 1,000 synthetic requests before confirming success.
5) If rollback validation fails, escalate to SRE on-call and hold route at 0% to problematic variant.

Manual postmortem additions:
- Run compatibility-diff to produce human-readable delta and attach to incident.
- Notify customers affected via customer-success runbook and share remediation timeline.

Schema validation configuration (table)

| Setting | Default | Description | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| schema.validation.enabled | true | Turn on validator in response-formatter | runtime-team |
| schema.validation.mode | strict | strict |runtime-team |
| schema.validation.sample_rate | 0.005 | Fraction of successful responses to validate for statistical coverage (0–1) | runtime-team |
| schema.mismatch.alert_threshold | 0.0005 | Fraction of requests triggering an alert (per minute) | SRE |
| schema.mismatch.auto_rollback | true | Allow automated walkback when thresholds breached | platform-ops |

Error types and client guidance

- 422 SchemaMismatch: the payload structure does not match requested schema. Clients should fallback to a compatible schema from Accept-Output-Schema or refresh their client library.
- 406 NotAcceptable: no compatible schema available; clients must request a supported schema list.
- 500 OutputGenerationError: generation failed before schema validation. Retry semantics: exponential backoff with jitter; max 3 retries.

Sample error response (422):

```json
{
  "error": "SchemaMismatch",
  "message": "Missing field: generation.metadata.language",
  "expected_schema": "v1.2",
  "available_schemas": ["v1.0", "v1.1", "v1.2"],
  "example_snippet": {"generation": {"text":"Example"}}
}
```

Client migration guidance

- For MINOR additions: use tolerant parsers and ignore unknown fields. Add explicit unit tests that parse the live API payloads periodically (weekly).
- For MAJOR renames/removals: opt-in migration mode via query param ?output_schema=v<MAJOR>.<MINOR> and schedule coordinated cutover windows. Notify customers two weeks in advance for enterprise tenants.

Telemetry and diagnostics checklist

- Ensure spans and logs include: schema.version, schema.validation.result, client.api_key_hash, model.version_alias.
- Export a daily compatibility report to /dashboards/schema-evolution with a 90-day rolling window.
- Retain one example capture per unique failing client per hour for 30 days (configurable).

Roles and responsibilities

- Runtime-team: implement header negotiation, validation hooks, and rollout tooling.
- Model-onboarding: author and publish schema definitions; tag model_catalog entries with supported_schemas metadata.
- SRE: define alert thresholds and own pager rotation for schema regressions.
- Customer-success: coordinate communication with customers impacted by MAJOR changes.

Decision log (when to do MAJOR vs MINOR)

- If the change alters field names or removes required fields -> MAJOR. Requires ADR + cross-team sign-off.
- If change is purely additive and consumers are expected to ignore unknown fields -> MINOR. Can be shipped with canary and automated gates.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets

- Validate new schema against previous: 
  tools/schema-compat check --old schema-v1.2.json --new schema-v1.3.json 

- Run canary batch locally (example):
  ./scripts/run_canary.sh --model alias:stable-v1 --schema v1.3 --sample prompts/canary-seed.csv

- Manual walkback trigger (admin CLI):
  rwctl model walkback --model-id model-abc --version v1.3 --reason "schema-mismatch-spike"
